info.title: Widgetic API Gateway
info.description: API documentation for the Widgetic API Gateway

get.description:
Lists the widgets your account owns, newest first. A widget is the reusable piece a composition is made
from; this is your own library, not a catalogue of Widgetic's widgets.

Pass `page` (counting from 1) and `size` (1 to 100, 20 when left out) to read the list one page at a time.
`meta` then carries `total`, `hasNextPage` and `hasPreviousPage`, so a client can walk the list to its end.
A page past the end is an empty list. Without `page` and `size` the call returns the whole list in one
response, which only suits an account with a few widgets.

Pass `canvasId` to list only the widgets on one of your canvases. That list is always returned whole,
whatever `page` and `size` say.

Pass `managedUserId` (Widgetic's id for one of your managed users) or `managedUserExternalId` (your own
identifier for the user) to list only the widgets made for that managed user. The widgets of your other
managed users, and your own, are left out. It combines with `page`, `size` and `canvasId`. A managed user
that is not yours, or does not exist, is answered with 404 and `MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return, counting from 1. Giving `page` or `size` turns paging on.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: How many widgets a page holds (20 when `page` is given without it). Giving `page` or `size` turns paging on.

parameters.name: canvasId
parameters.description: List only the widgets on this canvas. The list is returned whole.

parameters.name: managedUserId
parameters.description: List only the widgets made for this managed user (Widgetic's id for the user). Send this or `managedUserExternalId`, not both.

parameters.name: managedUserExternalId
parameters.description: List only the widgets made for the managed user you registered with this `external_id` (your own identifier for the user). Send this or `managedUserId`, not both.

meta.description:
Paging figures. On a whole-list answer they describe that one response (`page` 1, with
`size` and `total` both the number of widgets returned).

total.description: Every widget of the list, not only this page.

limit.description: The same as `size`, for clients that page by limit and offset.

offset.description: How many widgets come before this page.

400.description: A parameter is not valid (for example `size` above 100, a `canvasId` or `managedUserId` that is not a UUID, or both `managedUserId` and `managedUserExternalId`).

403.description: The key's role may not use this endpoint.

404.description: The managed user named by `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId` is not one of yours (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`).

429.description: Too many requests. See the Retry-After header.

post.description:
Creates a widget for your account: a named record with a type and some starting content, on a canvas of
its own (or one of yours that you name), with a database provisioned for it. It costs no credits and has no
code yet; the code is generated for it afterwards. The new widget is yours, and you can list it with
`getWidgets`. A widget is a draft until you say otherwise (`isDraft: false`).

If the database cannot be provisioned the widget is still created, and `data.warnings` says what did not
go through. Read it before relying on the widget.

A widget can be placed on one of your canvases (`canvasId`), in a project you can edit (`projectId`) or in an
organization where you may create widgets (`organizationId`). Naming anything you cannot use is refused
with 403, and the answer is the same whether it exists or not.

To make the widget for one of your managed users, send `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId`. The widget
stays in your account and is yours to edit; the tag lets you list one user's widgets with `getWidgets`. The
managed user must be yours and active: one that is not yours, or does not exist, is answered with 404 and
`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`, and one that is switched off with 409 and `MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`. The tag is set
here and does not change afterwards.

Creating a widget provisions its database, so this call has a limit of its own: 120 per minute for each
account (ask Widgetic if you need more). Past that the call is answered with 429 and a `Retry-After`.
The `Idempotency-Key` header is required; send the same key when you retry, so one widget is created, not
two.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value (a UUID is fine) that makes a retry of this request safe.

warnings.description: What did not go through, when the widget was created without all of its parts (for example, its database could not be provisioned). Absent when everything did.

400.description: Invalid request, or the `Idempotency-Key` header is missing.

403.description:
The key's role may not use this endpoint, or `canvasId`, `projectId` or `organizationId` names
something you may not use.

404.description: The managed user named by `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId` is not one of yours (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`).

409.description: The managed user is switched off, so nothing new can be made for it (`MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`).

429.description: Too many widgets created in a minute. See the Retry-After header.

x-codeSamples.source:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "net/http"
    "strings"
    "time"
)

func main() {
    payload := strings.NewReader(`{
  "name": "New Chart Widget",
  "type": "chart",
  "content": {
    "chartType": "bar",
    "dataSource": "api"
  },
  "isPublic": false,
  "isDraft": false,
  "canvasId": "abc12345-def6-7890-ab12-cd3456ef7890",
  "projectId": "7c1e2f30-4a5b-4c6d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
  "organizationId": "5e2d3f4a-1b6c-4a1f-8b9c-3c2d4e5f6a7b",
  "workspaceType": "personal",
  "managedUserId": "b7c8d9e0-1f2a-4b3c-8d4e-5f6a7b8c9d0e",
  "managedUserExternalId": "user-8841"
}`)
    request, err := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.widgetic.com/v1/widgets", payload)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error: %v\n", err)
        return
    }
    request.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY")
    request.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    request.Header.Set("Idempotency-Key", fmt.Sprintf("example-%d", time.Now().UnixNano()))

    response, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(request)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error: %v\n", err)
        return
    }
    defer response.Body.Close()

    body, _ := io.ReadAll(response.Body)
    fmt.Println(response.StatusCode, string(body))
}

post.summary: Create a composition for a widget in one call
post.description:
After a managed user publishes a widget from the creator, call this with the widget id, the customer's
managed user (when the widget is not already filed under one), and optional content, design, embed settings
and locale. Every input is validated before a single insert; a failure never leaves a half-made composition.

When the widget is already tagged with a managed user, you may omit `managed_user_id`. When you send it, it
must match that tag.

The widget must be published. The `Idempotency-Key` header is required.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The widget id

400.description: Validation failed (`VALIDATION_ERROR`)

403.description: Forbidden

404.description: Widget or managed user not found

409.description: Managed user inactive or widget not published

get.summary: List the websites allowed to show your widgets
get.description: Lists the websites on an account's own list, newest first. It is the list Widgetic checks when a widget of the account is embedded: when it holds at least one website, the widget is shown on those websites (and on Widgetic's own) and nowhere else; when it is empty, the widget can be shown anywhere. If the account administers a partner, the websites set on the partner record by Widgetic are added to them. Widgets that belong to an organization use the organization's list instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The account the list belongs to. For your own, your own user id

200.description: The websites on the list (an empty list when nothing is restricted)

403.description: The list belongs to another account

post.summary: Allow a website to show your widgets
post.description:
Adds a website to an account's own list. Give a website name such as `example.com`, or `*.example.com` for a website and all of its subdomains. A scheme, a port, a path, capital letters and a leading `www.` are dropped, so `https://www.Example.com/shop` is kept as `example.com`, and `example.com` covers `www.example.com` too. Something that is not a website name is refused, not stored.
Until the first website is added nothing is restricted, and a widget can be shown anywhere. Once the list has one, a widget of the account is shown on the listed websites (and on Widgetic's own) and nowhere else. A page on your own machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, on any port) is always allowed, so there is nothing to add to test locally. A change can take about 15 seconds to reach every server.
The list is a safeguard against other websites showing your widgets in a visitor's browser. It is not access control: anyone who knows a widget's id can still fetch its published content with a plain request that names no website.
An account can list at most 50 websites. Use `*.example.com` for a website and all of its subdomains instead of listing each one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The account the list belongs to. For your own, your own user id

400.description: The text is missing, longer than 255 characters, or not a website name

403.description: The list belongs to another account

409.description: The website is already on the list, or the list already holds 50 websites

post.description:
Makes a new API key for an account and returns its secret in `key`. That is the only time the secret is shown: Widgetic keeps a hash, so a key that was not stored cannot be recovered, only replaced. To rotate a key, make the new one, switch the integration over to it, then delete the old one.
Only a person signed in on widgetic.com can make a key: a request made with an API key, or with an SDK token, is refused with 403. That way a leaked key cannot be used to make a second one that survives its revocation. Make keys from the dashboard; a key can still list, rename, switch off and delete keys.
An `Idempotency-Key` header is required (8 to 50 characters: letters, digits, `-` and `_`). A retry with the same header and the same body returns the same answer instead of making a second key, and the same header with a different body is refused with 422. Make keys one at a time: two requests for the same account that run at the same moment can overwrite each other.
A key can be limited to what it needs. Send a `preset` (`read_only`, `content` or `full_access`) or a list of `scopes`, never both. Send neither for a key that can do everything its owner can, as every key made before scopes existed. A limited key is refused with 403 and the code `API_KEY_SCOPE_MISSING` on anything outside its scopes, so a key held by a build server or by a partner's backend can be given only the part of the API it uses. The scopes of a key are fixed when it is made: to widen one, make a new key and delete the old one. A limited key cannot make, change or delete keys, exchange tokens or reach the administration routes. The list of scopes is in the `ApiKeyScope` schema.
An account can hold at most 25 keys. An account on a plan without API access cannot make one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The account the key is for. For your own, your own user id

200.description: The key was made. The secret is in `key`, and is not shown again

400.description: The name, the expiry or the scopes are not valid (an unknown scope, an empty list, or both a preset and scopes), or the Idempotency-Key header is missing or malformed

403.description: The request was made with an API key or an SDK token (only a person signed in on widgetic.com can make a key), the account belongs to someone else, or its plan does not include API keys

409.description: The account already holds 25 keys, or another request with this Idempotency-Key is still running

422.description: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different body

put.description:
Renames a key, or switches it off (`isActive: false`) or back on. A key that is switched off is refused at once by the server that took the request and within a minute by the others, and can be switched on again; deleting is for a key that is not coming back. The secret, the expiry and the scopes of a key cannot be changed. Only a key with full access can make these requests: a key limited to some scopes is refused with 403 and the code `API_KEY_SCOPE_MISSING`.

post.description:
Stores one file for the account and returns its public address. This is how a user's own images,
video and PDFs reach a widget's content.

Send a `multipart/form-data` request with the file in the field named `file`. The file counts
against the account's storage allowance, and a full allowance is refused with 413 and
`QUOTA_STORAGE_EXCEEDED`. A file over the size limit is refused with 413 and `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, and a
type that is not accepted with 415 and `UPLOAD_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`; `uploadsLimitsGet` lists the size
limit and the accepted types.

To upload the file for one of your managed users, send `managed_user_id` (Widgetic's id for the user) or
`managed_user_external_id` (your own identifier for the user), not both. The file stays in your account and
counts against its allowance; the tag lets you list one user's files with `uploadsGet`. The managed user
must be yours and active: one that is not yours, or does not exist, is refused with 404 and
`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`, and one that is switched off with 409 and `MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`, before the
file is stored. The tag is set here and does not change afterwards.

Called with an editor session (`createManagedUserEditorSession`), the file is always filed for the
session's own managed user and is always media for widget content: naming another managed user is
refused with 403 and `MANAGED_USER_SESSION_MISMATCH`, and `context_type`, `source`, `widget_id` and
`conversation_id` are ignored. A full storage allowance is refused with the same 413 and
`QUOTA_STORAGE_EXCEEDED`, but the message only says that it is not available right now (not how much is
stored: that is the partner's business) and `error.details.limit` is `storage`.

An account that administers a partner with a storage destination (`setPartnerStorageDestination`) has
its files stored in the partner's own bucket instead. Such a file takes none of the allowance, its `url`
is served from the partner's public address, and its `storage_key` is the key in the partner's bucket.
The file is never stored with Widgetic instead: when the destination cannot be used the upload is refused
with 503 and `STORAGE_DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE`, and when the partner's storage rejects the file with
502 and `STORAGE_DESTINATION_WRITE_FAILED`.

Partner storage is not optional. A partner's own uploads (with its API key) and the uploads of its customers'
editor sessions are kept in the partner's own storage or not at all, so a partner with no destination (or
one that removed it after the session was made) has them refused with 409 and `PARTNER_STORAGE_REQUIRED`;
they are never stored with Widgetic. An editor session's browser is only told that the feature is not
available right now.

context_type.description: What the file is for. Send `content-property` for media that becomes widget content (images, video and PDF); the other values are used by Widgetic's own editor.

source.description: Which part of the product, or which client, the file comes from

managed_user_id.description: Upload the file for one of your managed users, by Widgetic's id for the user. Send this or `managed_user_external_id`, not both.

managed_user_external_id.description: The same, by your own identifier for the user, the `external_id` you gave when you created the managed user. Send this or `managed_user_id`, not both.

400.description: No file was sent, more than one was, or it was not in the field named `file`; or a managed user field is not valid (`MANAGED_USER_REFERENCE_INVALID`, or `MANAGED_USER_REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS` when both are sent)

401.description: The API key is missing or invalid

403.description: An editor session named a managed user other than its own (`MANAGED_USER_SESSION_MISMATCH`)

404.description: The managed user is not one of yours (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`)

409.description: The managed user is switched off, so nothing new can be uploaded for it (`MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`); or an editor session uploaded and the partner has no storage destination (`PARTNER_STORAGE_REQUIRED`)

413.description: The file is over the size limit (`UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE`), or the account's storage is full (`QUOTA_STORAGE_EXCEEDED`)

415.description: The file type is not accepted (`UPLOAD_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`)

502.description: The partner's own storage did not accept the file (`STORAGE_DESTINATION_WRITE_FAILED`)

503.description: The account's storage destination cannot be used right now (`STORAGE_DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE`)

put.summary: Set where a partner's uploaded files are stored
put.description:
Points the partner at a bucket of its own on an S3-compatible service (Amazon S3, Backblaze B2,
Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, MinIO and the like). From then on, a file uploaded with `uploadsPost` by the
account that administers the partner is stored in that bucket instead of with Widgetic. It takes none of
the account's storage allowance, and its `url` is served from `public_base_url`.

Only uploads sent with an API key, an SDK token or an editor session use the destination. Uploads from the
Widgetic website, resumable uploads and the media library keep using Widgetic's storage.

A destination is required. Partner storage is not optional: your customers' files, and your own uploads
with your API key, are kept in this destination and nowhere else. An editor session
(`createManagedUserEditorSession`) of any surface cannot be made until a destination is set (409
`PARTNER_STORAGE_REQUIRED`), a destination removed later stops the uploads of the sessions already made
(the same 409), and your own upload with no destination is refused in the same way instead of being stored
with Widgetic. A partner cannot be activated until it has a destination that works.

The destination is checked before it is saved. Widgetic writes a small test file under
`<key_prefix>widgetic-check/`, reads it back from `<public_base_url>/<its key>`, and deletes it. If any
step fails nothing is saved and the answer is 422 `STORAGE_DESTINATION_UNVERIFIED`: `details.step` says
where (`endpoint`, `write` or `public_read`), `details.reason` says why, and `param` names the field most
likely to be wrong.

What the bucket needs:
- an access key that may put objects into it (it may also delete objects, which lets the test file be
  cleaned up, but that is not required);
- its files publicly readable at `public_base_url`, either because the bucket is public or through a CDN.

The secret access key is stored encrypted and is never returned or logged; a response shows only the last
four characters of the access key id (`accessKeyHint`). Saving replaces the whole destination, so send
every field again, including the secret. Files already stored stay where they are, and keep working for
as long as that bucket stays publicly readable.

Once a destination is set, an upload is never stored with Widgetic instead: when the destination cannot be
used the upload is refused with 503 `STORAGE_DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE`, and when the bucket rejects the
file with 502 `STORAGE_DESTINATION_WRITE_FAILED`.

The caller must be the person who administers the partner (an API key of that account works); anyone else
is refused with 403 whether or not the partner exists. Widgetic administrators can set any partner's.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: The partner whose storage destination to set

200.description: The destination passed the check and was saved

400.description: A field is missing, malformed or not allowed. The error's param names it.

401.description: The API key is missing or invalid

403.description: The caller does not administer this partner

404.description: There is no such partner (reported to administrators only)

422.description: The destination did not pass the check (STORAGE_DESTINATION_UNVERIFIED). Nothing was saved.

429.description: Too many changes in a short time. Try again after the Retry-After seconds.

503.description: Storage destinations are not enabled on this server (PARTNER_STORAGE_DISABLED)

get.summary: List the widgets a partner offers as presets
get.description:
Returns the partner's presets, ordered by `position` and then by `key`: the widgets it offers its managed
users as starting points. The list is the same for every managed user.

Use a preset in one of two ways:
- **Make a composition of it** (the content and design editor): call `createComposition` with the preset's
  `widgetId` and the managed user. The widget itself stays yours; a composition is the user's own content.
- **Give the user a copy to build on** (the widget creator): call `copyPresetForManagedUser`. The user gets

(`setPartnerStorageDestination`). Use it to see which customers store the most, or to charge them for it.

get.summary: What was done with a partner's published widgets
get.description:
Counts what the visitors of the compositions made through your account did in a period: how many times a
composition was **viewed**, how many times a visitor **interacted** with one, and how many different visitors
there were. It covers every composition of your account, your own and the ones made for your managed users;
narrow it to one managed user with `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId` (not both).

The numbers come from the events the embedded widgets send while they are shown (the Widgetic embed SDK sends
them by itself), counted when you ask. Only views and interactions are counted; the events that describe a
visit (its start, its end, the device and the referrer) are not.

The period runs from `startDate` (included) to `endDate` (not included): the 30 days before now when you give
neither, and at most 366 days. A date without a time is midnight UTC at the start of that day, so for all of
October give `startDate=2026-10-01` and `endDate=2026-11-01`.

The caller must be the person who administers the partner (an API key of that account works, with the
`partner:read` scope), or a Widgetic administrator.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: The partner whose widgets to report on

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Start of the period, included. An ISO 8601 date (`2026-10-01`) or date-time with its offset (`2026-10-01T08:00:00Z`). Default 30 days before `endDate`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: End of the period, not included, in the same forms. Default now. It must be after `startDate`, by at most 366 days.

parameters.name: managedUserId
parameters.description: Report only on this managed user (Widgetic's id for the user). Send this or `managedUserExternalId`, not both.

parameters.name: managedUserExternalId
parameters.description: Report only on the managed user you registered with this `external_id` (your own identifier for the user). Send this or `managedUserId`, not both.

200.description: What was done with the widgets in the period

400.description: A date is not a date, `startDate` is not before `endDate`, the period is longer than 366 days, or the managed user is named wrongly

401.description: The API key is missing or invalid

403.description: The caller does not administer this partner

404.description: There is no such partner (reported to administrators only), or no managed user of yours matches (MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND)

put.description:
Changes who gets the emails, which events you want by email and by webhook, and the address of your webhook.
A key you leave out of the body is left as it was; send only what changes.

**Email.** `emailRecipients` is the list of addresses (at most five). While it is empty the emails about
invoices go to the billing emails of your billing profile (your contact email when there are none), and the
others to your contact email. The events about money and about the standing of your account are always
emailed, whatever `emailEvents` says; it narrows the others.

**Webhook.** `webhookUrl` is where Widgetic sends a signed `POST` for each event, so that your own system
can act on it (mark an invoice paid, warn your team that credits are low). The address must be `https` on the
standard port, on a public site, and must not redirect. Setting an address when you have no secret yet makes
one, and the answer carries it as `webhookSecret`: **keep it now, it is shown once**. `webhookEvents` narrows
what is sent.

Each call has a JSON body, `{ "id": "evt_...", "type": "invoice.paid", "createdAt": "...", "partnerId": "...",
"data": { ... } }` (`data` is the `data` of `PartnerNotification`), and these headers:
`webhook-id` (the same as `id`, and the same on every retry), `webhook-timestamp` (seconds since 1970) and
`webhook-signature` (`v1,` and a base64 HMAC-SHA256). It is the Standard Webhooks scheme, so any of its
libraries verifies it. By hand: take your secret without the `whsec_` prefix, decode it from base64, and sign
the text `<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<the raw body>` with it; the header holds `v1,<base64 of the
result>` (two signatures separated by a space while a rotated secret overlaps). Reject a `webhook-timestamp`
that is more than five minutes old.

Answer with a 2xx status within ten seconds. Anything else is tried again, eight attempts in all over about
two days (`listPartnerNotificationDeliveries` shows each). Delivery is at least once: if your answer was lost
the same event arrives again with the same `id`, so drop what you have already handled by it.

Changing the settings needs an API key with full access: they decide where your notifications go.
The caller must be the person who administers the partner, or a Widgetic administrator.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: The partner whose notification settings to change

400.description: A value is missing, malformed or not allowed (INVALID_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS). `error.details.problems` names each field and says why. Nothing was saved.

401.description: The API key is missing or invalid

403.description: The caller does not administer this partner, or the API key has not full access

404.description: There is no such partner (reported to administrators only)

429.description: Too many changes in a short time. Try again after the Retry-After seconds.

503.description: Webhooks cannot be set up on this server right now (WEBHOOK_SIGNING_UNAVAILABLE). Nothing was changed.

get.description:
Follows work that carries on after the response that started it. Duplicating a composition,
for one, answers 202 with an `operationId`: ask for that operation until its `status` is
`completed` (or `failed`, with the reason in `error`). A finished duplication names the new
composition in `metadata.newCompositionId`.

An operation belongs to the user who started it. Asking for somebody else's operation answers
404, exactly as for one that does not exist. Administrators may read any operation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Operation identifier returned when the job was created.

schema.description: Operation payload including status, metadata, and timestamps.

id.description: The operation's identifier, the `operationId` the call that started it returned

status.description: Where the operation stands. `completed`, `failed` and `cancelled` are final

progress.description: How far the operation has got, in percent

metadata.description: What the operation tells about its work. A finished composition duplication names the new composition in `newCompositionId`, and lists any problem with its database in `warnings` (absent when there is none).

404.description: Operation not found, or started by someone else.

get.description:
The notices that currently apply to the caller: their own, plus those of
the organizations they own or administer. Expired and dismissed notices are
never returned, so a client can render what it receives without filtering.

Two producers today. The free plan's window closing: an account that never
subscribed stops having its published embeds served when its 7-day window
ends (`embedServingGate`). And a failed payment on an organization's
subscription (`organizationDunningNoticeService`): shown to the
organization's owners and admins, because the card is theirs to fix and the
email that says so may not be read before the dunning window closes. Both
are raised by the server for conditions it observed, never by a client.

post.summary: Create an editor session for a managed user
post.description:
Makes a short-lived credential that lets the browser of ONE of your managed users use Widgetic's editor
pieces, such as the File Browser and the composition editor, without your API key ever reaching that
browser. Call this from your server when the page that hosts the editor opens, and hand the `token` in
the answer to that page.

The token is shown once. It starts with `wgt_ses_` and the browser sends it as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It can do only what the `surfaces` you name allow, and only for this
managed user:

- `files`: upload a file (`uploadsPost`) and list the files uploaded for this user (`uploadsGet`). Every
  file is filed for this user and stored in your own storage destination, never in Widgetic's: a file a
  customer uploads is yours to keep, and takes none of your storage allowance. Partner storage is not
  optional, so no session, whatever its surfaces, can be made until you have set a destination
  (`setPartnerStorageDestination`); until then it is refused with 409 and `PARTNER_STORAGE_REQUIRED`, and
  when the destination cannot be used with 503 and `STORAGE_DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE`. A destination you
  remove after the session was made stops its uploads too (the same 409; the browser is only told that
  the feature is not available right now). To keep a customer from uploading, leave `files` out of the
  session and hand the editors your own media library instead (`mediaLibrary`).
- `editor`: edit one of this user's compositions: read it (`getCompositionById`, its content, design,
  embed settings and schemas), check a content change (`validateCompositionContent`), and change its
  name, content, design and embed settings (`updateComposition`, `setDynamicContent`). It can reach
  only compositions you created for this managed user (tag them with `managedUserId` when you create
  them); any other composition, including another of your users', answers 404.
- `creator`: use Widgetic's widget creator for this user, including its AI. Draw on canvases and save
  them (`getAllCanvases`, `getCanvas`, `createCanvas`, `updateCanvas`, `previewDeleteCanvas`,
  `deleteCanvas`); make, change, copy and delete the widgets on them (`createWidget`, `getWidgets`,
  `getWidgetsBatch`, `updateWidget`, `uploadWidgetThumbnail`, `duplicateWidget`, `deleteWidget`);
  list and make the compositions of a widget it built (`getAllCompositions`, `createComposition`), which
  is how it shows the widget with sample values; read and add their
  components (`getComponentsByWidgetId`, `createComponent`); keep the
  conversation of each widget (`getConversationsByWidgetId`, `createConversationForWidget`,
  `updateConversation`, `getMessages`, `createMessage`, `updateMessage`, `restoreCheckpoint`); and read a
  widget's schemas and give it its repository (`getWidgetContentSchema`, `getWidgetDesignSchema`,
  `updateWidgetRepository`). The AI that builds a widget is part of it: list the models
  (`agentModelsGet`), open the widget's repository (`agentRepositoriesPost`,
  `agentRepositoriesRepoIdGet`), start a generation and follow or cancel it (`agentCodeGeneratePost`,
  `operationsStreamGet`, `operationsIdGet`, `operationsIdCancelPost`), build and preview the result
  (`agentWidgetBuilderRepoHeadWidgetIdGet`, `buildWidgetFromRepo`, `previewWidgetVersion`), publish a
  version of the widget and move between its versions (`agentWidgetBuilderPublishWidgetIdPost`,
  `getWidgetPublishHistory`, `setWidgetPublishHistoryLive`, `renameWidgetPublishHistoryTitle`), and
  turn a stroke or a sentence into a decision (`agentShapeRecognizePost`, `agentDesignResolvePost`). It can
  also offer the customer your presets as starting points: read them and ask for a copy for this customer
  (`listMyPresets`, `copyMyPreset`; you choose the presets with `setPartnerPreset`).
  What the session makes is filed for this managed user, and the lists it reads hold only this user's
  canvases, widgets and compositions. It can reach only canvases, widgets, compositions, repositories,
  uploaded files and operations made for this managed user (tag the canvases and widgets you create
  with `managedUserId`); any other canvas, widget, composition, conversation, message, repository, file
  or operation, including another of your users', answers 404. The creator also saves the composition
  it is editing (`updateComposition`, from the `editor` surface) and attaches pictures to its chat
  (`uploadsPost`, from the `files` surface), and the surfaces do not imply one another: to open the
  whole creator for a user, ask for `creator`, `editor` and `files` together. A generation or a build
  one user starts can be followed and cancelled by that user and by you, never by another of your
  users. The AI is paid for by your account, as your own calls are: its credits and allowances are
  yours. A session cannot make a widget public (publishing a version does not), file one under a
  project or an organization, or set anything the creator does not set: a body with another field is
  refused with 403 and `EDITOR_SESSION_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED`.

Everything else is refused with 403 and `EDITOR_SESSION_ROUTE_NOT_ALLOWED`: a session cannot read your
account, make more sessions, change your presets or delete a composition, and a session without the `creator` surface cannot
create or list compositions. Create the composition yourself with your API key, then open the editor on it.

A session ends at `expiresAt` (at most four hours), when you end it (`revokeManagedUserEditorSession`),
or when the managed user is switched off or deleted. A managed user can have at most 100 live sessions at
once (`429 EDITOR_SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED`). A session that is bound to a web page (`allowed_origin`) is
refused from any other origin.

The AI the session runs is paid for with your credits. Set `max_credits` to hold the session to a number
of them: once its generations have taken that many (a generation that fails is refunded and does not
count), the next one is refused with 402 and `EDITOR_SESSION_CREDIT_LIMIT_REACHED`, and the browser is told
only that the feature is not available right now. Without it, the limit Widgetic has set for your account
applies when it has set one (the same limit for every session you make, and `max_credits: null` asks for
none), and otherwise the credits of your account are the only ceiling. What each of your users' sessions
has spent is in `getManagedUserUsage`.

Each call makes a new session. It does not take an `Idempotency-Key`: the answer holds the token, and
the token is never stored where a retry could read it back. The answer is sent with
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The managed user the session is for (Widgetic's id for the user)

201.description: The session, with its token (shown once)

400.description: A surface is not one that exists, `expires_in_seconds` or `max_credits` is out of range, or `allowed_origin` is not an origin

403.description: Forbidden - the caller is not a partner, or Widgetic has switched editor sessions off for your account (`EDITOR_SESSIONS_DISABLED_FOR_PARTNER`)

404.description: No managed user with this id on your account (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`). Another partner's managed user answers 404 as well.

409.description: The managed user is switched off, so no session can be made for it (`MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`); or you have not set a storage destination (`PARTNER_STORAGE_REQUIRED`)

429.description: The managed user already has the most live sessions allowed (`EDITOR_SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED`)

503.description: Editor sessions are switched off for the moment (`EDITOR_SESSIONS_DISABLED`), or your storage destination cannot be used (`STORAGE_DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE`). Try again later.

get.summary: What a managed user's editor sessions spent
get.description:
Says how many credits the editor sessions of one of your managed users took from your account over a
period, in total and for each operation. A generation costs one credit, taken from your account when it
starts; one that fails is refunded and is counted as refunded, not as spent.

Only what was spent through editor sessions is here, and only since usage was first recorded: what you
spend with your API key, and anything from before, is not. Use it to see which of your users spend the
most, or to charge them for it. To hold one session to a number of credits, set `max_credits` when you
make it (`createManagedUserEditorSession`).

The period runs from `startDate` (included) to `endDate` (not included): the 30 days before now when you
give neither, and at most 366 days. A date without a time is midnight UTC at the start of that day, so for
all of October give `startDate=2026-10-01` and `endDate=2026-11-01`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The managed user whose usage you want (Widgetic's id for the user)

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Start of the period, included: an ISO 8601 date (`2026-10-01`) or date-time with its offset (`2026-10-01T08:00:00Z`). Default: 30 days before `endDate`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: End of the period, not included, in the same forms. Default: now. It must be after `startDate`, by at most 366 days.

200.description: What the managed user's editor sessions spent in the period

400.description: A date is not a date, `startDate` is not before `endDate`, or the period is longer than 366 days

403.description: Forbidden - the caller is not a partner

404.description: No managed user with this id on your account (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`). Another partner's managed user answers 404 as well.

post.summary: Give a managed user a copy of one of your presets
post.description:
Copies the preset `key` (see `setPartnerPreset`) onto a new canvas for one of your managed users, so their
widget creator opens on a widget of their own that starts from yours. The copy is a draft widget in your
account, filed under the managed user: `getAllWidgets` with `managedUserId` lists it, and no other managed
user's editor can reach it.

The copy carries the preset's code, design and content schemas, and thumbnail, and starts from a fork of its
code repository, so the user's chat edits begin where yours left off. It does not carry the preset's
database or its compositions. It is not a preset itself, and changing or removing the preset afterwards
never touches it.

To start a composition (the content and design editor) instead, you do not need a copy: call
`createComposition` with the preset's `widgetId` (from `listPartnerPresets`) and the managed user.

The `Idempotency-Key` header is required (`400` without it). Send the same key when you retry, so one copy
is made, not two. A copy that could not be made leaves nothing behind (503 `PRESET_COPY_FAILED`).

The managed user must be yours and active.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The managed user to give the copy to (Widgetic's id for the user)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key of the preset to copy

400.description: The key or the name is malformed, or the Idempotency-Key header is missing

403.description: Forbidden - the caller is not a partner

404.description: No such managed user on your account (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`), or no preset with this key (`PRESET_NOT_FOUND`)

409.description: The managed user is switched off, so nothing new can be made for it (`MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`)

503.description: The copy could not be made right now (`PRESET_COPY_FAILED`). Nothing was created; ask again.

get.description:
Lists the invoices issued to a partner, newest first. Each carries the price (`subtotal`), the tax on
it (`taxAmount`) and what is paid (`total`), its status as the payment provider reports it, why the
last payment failed (`failureReason`), and the page where it is paid (`hostedInvoiceUrl`).

A partner reads its own: the caller must be the person who administers the partner (an API key of
that account works), and anyone else is refused with 403 whether or not the partner exists.
Widgetic administrators can read any partner's and see exactly what the partner sees; the full
records, with the internal fields, are `getAllInvoices` filtered by partner.

The page is always bounded: `limit` defaults to 50 and is capped at 100, `offset` defaults to 0.

parameters.description: Maximum number of invoices to return

parameters.name: offset

get.description:
Lists the entries of an account's credit ledger, newest first. This is also how an account's usage is
read: every operation that spends credits is a `debit` entry, so summing the `debit` entries over a
period gives the credits consumed in it, and the other types give what was added.

An account reads its own ledger; with a partner's API key, that is the account of the person who
administers the partner. Widgetic administrators can read any account's. A partner's wallet is a
separate ledger, read with `getPartnerCreditTransactions`.

The page is always bounded: `limit` defaults to 100 and is capped at 500, `offset` defaults to 0.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The account whose ledger to read

parameters.name: transaction_type
parameters.description: Only entries of this type, for instance `debit` for the credits spent. The types are listed on `AccountCreditTransaction`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of entries to skip

200.description: The account's ledger entries, newest first

401.description: The API key is missing or invalid

403.description: The ledger belongs to another account

get.description:
Retrieves all compositions with pagination support.

Pass `managedUserId` (Widgetic's id for one of your managed users) or `managedUserExternalId` (your own
identifier for the user) to list only the compositions made for that managed user. The compositions of
your other managed users, and your own, are left out. It combines with the other filters and with paging.
A managed user that is not yours, or does not exist, is answered with 404 and `MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`.

An editor session with the `creator` surface may call this to list the compositions of ONE widget it
built: it must send `widget_id`, and the answer holds only the compositions made for the session's
managed user.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of items per page

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field and direction (e.g., "createdAt:desc")

parameters.name: widget_id
parameters.description: Filter compositions by widget ID

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Filter by workspace

parameters.name: project_folder
parameters.description: Filter by project folder

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by composition status

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated related resources to include

parameters.name: managedUserId
parameters.description: List only the compositions made for this managed user (Widgetic's id for the user). Send this or `managedUserExternalId`, not both. Spelled in camelCase, unlike `widget_id`; the snake_case spelling `managed_user_id` is refused with a 400, not ignored.

parameters.name: managedUserExternalId
parameters.description: List only the compositions made for the managed user you registered with this `external_id` (your own identifier for the user). Send this or `managedUserId`, not both.

400.description: A parameter is not valid (for example a `managedUserId` that is not a UUID, or both `managedUserId` and `managedUserExternalId`).

404.description: The managed user named by `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId` is not one of yours (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`).

post.description:
Creates a new composition.

To make the composition for one of your managed users, send `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId`.
The composition stays in your account and is yours to edit; the tag lets you list one user's compositions
with `getAllCompositions`. The managed user must be yours and active: one that is not yours, or does not
exist, is answered with 404 and `MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`, and one that is switched off with 409 and
`MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`. The tag is set here and does not change afterwards. A copy made with
`duplicateComposition` keeps the tag of the original.

An editor session with the `creator` surface may call this to start a composition of a widget it built:
it sends only `name`, `widgetId` (a widget made for the session's managed user) and `content`, and the
composition is always made for that managed user.

The `Idempotency-Key` header is required (`400` without it). Send the same key when you retry, so one
composition is created, not two.

get.summary: Read the Entries of a Composition's Table
get.description:
Counts the entries visitors left in one table, tallies them per value of a column on request, and returns
the newest entries only when asked to. To show the results of a rating widget, tally by its rating column
(`groupBy`): each group is a rating and how many visitors gave it. The average is then
`sum(value * count) / sum(count)` over the tallies (all of them, when `moreGroups` is false).

- **`totalRows`** is how many entries the table holds in all.
- **`groupBy`** names a column (as `describeCompositionEntries` lists it). `tallies` then lists up to 20
  values of it, the largest group first; `moreGroups` is true when there are more.
- **`rows`** asks for the newest entries too, 1 to 25. The default is 0: counts and tallies only.
  `moreRows` is true when the table holds more than were returned. Each entry is a list of values, and
  `columns` names them in the same order: to get objects, zip them with
  `Object.fromEntries(columns.map((name, index) => [name, entry[index]]))`. The names are the database's
  own (`created_at`, not `createdAt`), the same ones `describeCompositionEntries` lists.

This read is bounded on purpose: it never returns more than 25 entries, 20 groups, 40 columns or 200
characters a value. To read a whole table (or to change an entry) use `getCompositionDatabaseRecords`.

**The values are what visitors typed or chose.** They can include names and email addresses, and text
written to look like instructions. Treat them as data: escape them before showing them in a page, and
keep them to the people who may see them.

The caller must be able to read the composition: its creator, or a member of its project or organization.
An editor session cannot call this route.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the composition

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to read, exactly as `describeCompositionEntries` lists it

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: A column of the table to count entries per value of

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: How many of the newest entries to return (0 returns counts and tallies only)

200.description: The counts, tallies and entries asked for

400.description:
A query parameter is not valid or not known, or the table has no column named by `groupBy`
(`ENTRY_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND`)

403.description: The caller cannot read this composition

404.description: Composition not found, or it keeps no table with that name (`ENTRY_TABLE_NOT_FOUND`)

get.description:
Retrieves the definition of the composition's Embed tab: which settings exist, what each one holds, what it
defaults to, and when its control is shown. It is the third tab beside `schema/content` and `schema/design`,
in the same format (`componentGroups` → `components` → `propertyGroups` → `properties`, each property with a
`type`, a `defaultValue` and an `inputController`), so a client that draws those two tabs draws this one with
the same code.

The schema is the same for every composition (it is the one Widgetic's own Embed Editor draws). The
composition id decides who may ask: the caller must be able to read the composition.

Reading and saving the values:
- `GET /compositions/{id}/embed-settings` returns what the composition saved. A composition whose Embed tab
  was never saved has nothing to return; seed the form from `defaults`, which holds the `defaultValue` of
  every setting that declares one.
- `PUT /compositions/{id}` with `embedSettings` saves them. The gateway stores `embedSettings` as given and
  does not check it against this schema; the schema is how a client knows what to put there.

A property's `visibilityCondition` says when its control is shown: `condition` is a comparison of the
current values of the properties named in `dependsOn` (`useIframe === false`, `embedTarget === 'mixed' &&
keepDimensions === false`). While it is false the Embed Editor does not show the control.

A colour picker with `showOpacityControls` saves its opacity next to the colour, under the key
`<name>_opacity` as a number from 0 to 1 (`overlayBackgroundColor` → `overlayBackgroundColor_opacity`).
Its `defaultTransparency` is a percentage and the saved value a fraction (50 → 0.5).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the composition

version.description: Version of the schema; it changes when a setting is added, removed or retyped

componentGroups.description: The controls of the Embed tab, grouped as the editor shows them

defaults.description:
The value of every setting that declares one, by setting name. A value is a boolean, a number or a
string, as the setting's `type` says. (Written as an open map, not as a choice of three types: a
generated client cannot be built from a choice between plain types.)

403.description: The caller cannot read this composition

post.description:
Retrieves multiple compositions by their IDs in a single request.
This endpoint includes domain validation for embed contexts and is used by the embed SDK.

Each composition is checked on its own. If its owner listed the websites it may appear on (the
workspace's domain list, or the `allowedDomains` of a partner the owner administers) and the request
comes from another website (the `Origin` header, or the host of `Referer` when there is no `Origin`),
that composition is left out of `compositions` and reported in `errors` as
`Domain access denied: <reason>`; the others are still returned. A request that names no website, and
an owner who listed nothing, are not restricted, and a page on the visitor's own machine (`localhost`,
`127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, on any port) is always allowed.

compositionIds.description: Array of composition IDs to retrieve

get.description:
Retrieves all canvases with pagination support and filtering options.

Pass `managedUserId` (Widgetic's id for one of your managed users) or `managedUserExternalId` (your own
identifier for the user) to list only the canvases made for that managed user. The canvases of your other
managed users, and your own, are left out. A managed user that is not yours, or does not exist, is answered
with 404 and `MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`. Called with an editor session, the list is always the session's
managed user's.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of items per page

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field and direction (e.g., "created_at:desc")

parameters.name: component_id
parameters.description: Filter canvases by a specific component ID

parameters.name: widget_components
parameters.description: Filter canvases by widget components ID

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Filter canvases created after the specified date (ISO 8601 format)

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Filter canvases created before the specified date (ISO 8601 format)

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Filter canvases updated after the specified date (ISO 8601 format)

parameters.name: updated_before
parameters.description: Filter canvases updated before the specified date (ISO 8601 format)

parameters.name: managedUserId
parameters.description: List only the canvases made for this managed user (Widgetic's id for the user). Send this or `managedUserExternalId`, not both.

parameters.name: managedUserExternalId
parameters.description: List only the canvases made for the managed user you registered with this `external_id` (your own identifier for the user). Send this or `managedUserId`, not both.

total.description: Total number of canvases matching the criteria

400.description: A parameter is not valid (for example a `managedUserId` that is not a UUID, or both `managedUserId` and `managedUserExternalId`).

404.description: The managed user named by `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId` is not one of yours (`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`).

To make the canvas for one of your managed users, send `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId`. The canvas
stays in your account and is yours to edit; the tag lets you list one user's canvases with `getAllCanvases`.
The managed user must be yours and active: one that is not yours, or does not exist, is answered with 404 and
`MANAGED_USER_NOT_FOUND`, and one that is switched off with 409 and `MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`. The tag is set
here and does not change afterwards. Called with an editor session, the canvas is always made for the
session's managed user.

409.description: The managed user is switched off, so nothing new can be made for it (`MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`).

PersonalWorkspaceDomain.description: One website on a person's own list of the websites allowed to show their widgets

id.description: The id of the entry. Use it to change or remove the entry

userId.description: The account the list belongs to

domain.description: The website as it is kept: lower case, with no scheme, port, path or leading `www.`. A leading `*.` means the website and all of its subdomains

ApiKeyScope.description:
One thing an API key may be allowed to do. A key made with a list of scopes does only what the list
names; a key made without one has full access, and does everything its owner can.

- `content:read` reads widgets, compositions, canvases, projects, folders, uploads, translations and the
  analytics of your content.
- `content:write` creates, changes, publishes and deletes the same. It includes `content:read`.
- `generate` runs the AI that builds widgets and compositions, and follows or cancels what it is doing.
  This spends credits.
- `partner:read` reads managed users, what they spent, presets, the contract and the storage destination.
- `partner:write` creates, changes and deletes managed users and presets. It includes `partner:read`.
- `billing:read` reads credits, usage, invoices, subscriptions and payment methods.
- `billing:write` buys credits, pays invoices and changes a subscription or a payment method. It
  includes `billing:read`.
- `account:read` reads the profile, organizations and members, allowed domains, notices and the names
  of API keys.
- `account:write` changes the profile, organizations and members, allowed domains and integrations. It
  includes `account:read`.

Starting an editor session for a managed user needs `partner:write`, `content:write` and `generate`
together. Making, changing and deleting keys, exchanging tokens, signing in and the administration
routes need full access: a limited key cannot make itself a bigger one.

A request outside the scopes of the key is refused with 403 and the code `API_KEY_SCOPE_MISSING`.
`error.details.missingScopes` names what a new key needs, and `error.details.fullAccessRequired` is true
when no list of scopes would have been enough. The scopes of a key cannot be changed once it is made.

UserApiKey.description: An API key of an account, as it is listed. It never carries the secret: that is shown once, in the answer to the request that made the key, and cannot be read again.

keyId.description: The id of the key. Use it to rename, switch off, delete or read the usage of the key

keyPreview.description: The first characters of the key, to tell keys apart. Not enough to use it

name.description: The name given to the key

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working. Absent or null when it does not expire

lastUsedAt.description: When the key was last used. Absent or null when it never was

isActive.description: Whether the key works. A key that is switched off is refused until it is switched on again

scopes.description: What the key may do. A key with full access holds every scope. The scopes of a key are fixed when it is made

preset.description: The name the scopes amount to. `full_access` is a key that is not limited, `read_only` and `content` are the ready-made lists, and `custom` is any other list

CreatedUserApiKey.description: A key that has just been made. It is the only answer that ever carries the secret, in `key`. Store it now: Widgetic keeps only a hash of it, and it cannot be shown again.

key.description: The secret. Send it as a bearer token, in the `Authorization` header. Shown once

scopes.description: What the key may do. A key made without scopes holds every scope

preset.description: The name the scopes amount to

name.description: A name for the key, to tell it from the account's other keys

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working, as a date and time in the future with a zone. Omit it for a key that does not expire

preset.description: A ready-made list of scopes. `read_only` looks at everything the account holds and changes nothing. `content` builds and manages widgets and compositions and runs the AI, and touches no billing, no people and no partners. `full_access` is the same as sending neither `preset` nor `scopes`. Send either `preset` or `scopes`, not both

scopes.description: What the key may do, when a preset is not enough. Naming a write scope includes its read scope, and a list that holds every scope is a key with full access. Send either `scopes` or `preset`, not both

UpdateUserApiKeyRequest.description: At least one of the two is required

name.description: A new name. It cannot be one that another key of the account already has

isActive.description: false switches the key off, true switches it on again. A key that is switched off stops working within a minute at the latest, and at once on the server that took the request

UserApiKeyUsageLog.description: One call made with a key

keyId.description: The key the call was made with

status.description: The HTTP status the call ended with

details.description: What was recorded about the call

Upload.description: A file stored for the account that uploaded it.

url.description: The public address of the stored file

mime_type.description: The type of the stored file. A HEIC or HEIF photo is stored as `image/jpeg`.

file_size.description: Size of the stored file, in bytes

storage_key.description: Where the file sits in its storage bucket

context_type.description: What the file was uploaded for. Media for widget content is `content-property`.

source.description: Which part of the product, or which client, uploaded the file

managed_user_id.description: The managed user the file was uploaded for, or null when it is the account's own. List one managed user's files with the `managed_user_id` or `managed_user_external_id` query parameter of `uploadsGet`.

UploadLimits.description: What the upload endpoints accept. Read it rather than hard-coding the numbers.

multipart_max_bytes.description: The largest file `uploadsPost` takes in one request, in bytes. The same for every account.

multipart_mime_types.description: The file types `uploadsPost` takes for media (`content-property` uploads)

tus_enabled.description: Whether resumable uploads are switched on. They need a signed-in session; an API key uses `uploadsPost`.

tus_max_bytes.description: The largest file a resumable upload takes, in bytes (250 MB by default). The same for every account, whatever its plan. A file over `multipart_max_bytes` goes through a resumable upload.

tus_chunk_size_bytes.description: The chunk size resumable uploads are tuned for, in bytes. A client may send smaller or larger chunks.

MyPartner.description: A partner as the person who administers it reads it: which partner it is, what standing it is in, and why it is paused when it is. The webhook address, its secret and the billing settings have their own routes and are not part of it.

id.description: The id every other partner route asks for (`/partners/{partnerId}/...`)

status.description: `active` while the partner is in force. `inactive` until Widgetic activates it (and after a deactivation). `suspended` while it is paused, which is done by hand and comes back when Widgetic resumes it.

allowedDomains.description: The domains Widgetic added to the embeds of this partner's customers. The domains the person added themselves are on the domains route of the account.

suspendedAt.description: When the partner was paused; null unless it is paused now

suspensionReason.description: The reason given when the partner was paused, as the partner is told it; null unless it is paused now

standing.description: The standing of the account as a whole, the word every gate reads: `not_a_partner` when the account administers no partner; otherwise `active` when any of its partners is active, else `suspended` when any is paused, else `inactive`.

partners.description: The partners the account administers (nearly always one), the oldest first

PartnerContract.description: The commercial terms agreed with a partner. Prices are in dollars. Internal negotiation notes and the staff members who edited the record are not part of it.

customPrice.description: The agreed price per `billingCycle`; null when the standard price applies

customCredits.description: Credits included per cycle; null when the standard allowance applies

customStorageGb.description: Storage included, in gigabytes; null when the standard allowance applies

additionalFeatures.description: Features included beyond the standard partner plan

contractEndDate.description: Null when the contract runs until it is ended

isActiveContract.description: True while the contract is in force, that is when it is open-ended or today falls between its start and end

PartnerStorageDestination.description: The bucket a partner keeps the files its account uploads in: a bucket on an S3-compatible service that the partner owns. The secret access key is never returned.

endpoint.description: The HTTPS address of the S3-compatible service, scheme and host only

keyPrefix.description: The folder inside the bucket every file is written under. Empty, or folders each followed by a slash.

publicBaseUrl.description: Where the stored files are served from. A file's url is this address, a slash and the file's key.

forcePathStyle.description: Whether the bucket name goes in the path of a request (true) or in the host name (false)

accessKeyHint.description: The last four characters of the access key id, to tell which key is set. Not enough to use it.

verifiedAt.description: When the destination last passed the check

lastVerificationError.description: Why the most recent re-check failed. Null while the last check passed.

SetPartnerStorageDestinationRequest.description: The bucket to keep the partner's files in, and the key that may write to it. These field names are snake_case, as in every request.

endpoint.description: The HTTPS address of the S3-compatible service, scheme and host only (no path, port or credentials). It must be a host name, not an IP address, and must resolve to the public internet.

region.description: The region the service signs requests for. Use auto where the service says so.

key_prefix.description: A folder inside the bucket to write every file under, for example widgetic/uploads. Folders are made of letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores. Leave it out to write at the root of the bucket.

public_base_url.description: Where the stored files are served from: the bucket's public address, or a CDN in front of it. The address of a file is this value, a slash and the file's key in the bucket, which starts with the key prefix. A path is allowed (https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/acme-widget-media).

force_path_style.description: Put the bucket name in the path of a request. Every S3-compatible service supports this; set it to false only for a service that needs the bucket name in the host name.

access_key_id.description: The id of an access key that may put objects into the bucket

secret_access_key.description: The secret of that access key. It is stored encrypted and is never returned.

removed.description: False when the partner had no storage destination to remove

PartnerPreset.description: A widget the partner offers its managed users as a starting point, under a key the partner's code names. It belongs to the partner's account, so every managed user of the partner sees the same list.

key.description: The name the partner's code uses for the preset

widgetId.description: The partner's widget. Use it to make a composition (`createComposition` with this `widgetId`).

title.description: What the partner's picker shows. Null means show `widgetName`.

position.description: The list is ordered by this, smallest first, then by key

thumbnailUrl.description: The widget's thumbnail, when it has one

widgetId.description: One of the partner's own widgets. A widget is a preset under at most one key.

title.description: What your picker shows. Leave it out to show the widget's own name.

position.description: Where the preset sits in the list. Smallest first; presets with the same position are ordered by key.

removed.description: False when there was no preset under that key

PartnerReportPage.description: Which part of a list the answer holds.

limit.description: How many rows the page can hold at most

offset.description: How many rows were skipped before this page

hasMore.description: True when more rows follow this page. Ask again with `offset` raised by `limit`.

PartnerReportPeriod.description: The stretch of time a report covers.

to.description: End of the period, not included

PartnerStorageUsageTotals.description: What a group of files weigh, and how much of it is kept where.

totalBytes.description: The size of all the files together, in bytes

widgeticStorageBytes.description: The part of `totalBytes` that is kept in Widgetic's storage

partnerStorageBytes.description: The part of `totalBytes` that is kept in your own storage destination

PartnerStorageUsageOfManagedUser.description: The files filed under one managed user. The row with a null `managedUserId` is the files that are not filed under any: your own, and the ones uploaded without naming a managed user.

managedUserId.description: Widgetic's id for the managed user. Null for the files that are not filed under one.

externalId.description: Your own identifier for the managed user

isActive.description: False when the managed user is switched off

lastUploadAt.description: When the newest of these files was stored

PartnerStorageUsage.description: What a partner's customers store. `totals` is every file kept for the partner's account; `managedUsers` splits it by the managed user each file is filed under, the heaviest first.

PartnerAnalyticsSummary.description: What was done with the partner's published widgets in a period.

managedUserId.description: The managed user the report is narrowed to. Null for the whole account.

views.description: How many times a composition was shown to a visitor

interactions.description: How many times a visitor did something with a composition

managedUsersViewed.description: How many different managed users had a composition viewed

PartnerAnalyticsOfManagedUser.description: What one managed user's widgets and compositions did in a period.

externalId.description: Your own identifier for the managed user

widgetsMade.description: How many widgets are filed under the managed user (all time, not only in the period)

lastEventAt.description: When the newest counted view or interaction happened. Null when there was none in the period.

widgetName.description: Null when the widget has been deleted since

managedUserId.description: The managed user the report is narrowed to. Null for the whole account.

PartnerNotificationEventType.description: What happened. The event types you can be told about.

PartnerNotification.description: One thing that happened to your partner account. The same object is what your webhook receives as `data` of a call (beside `id`, `type`, `createdAt` and `partnerId`), and what the list in your dashboard shows.

body.description: A few sentences that say what happened and what to do about it

data.description: The facts of the event, named in camelCase. An invoice event carries `invoiceNumber`, `subtotal`, `taxAmount`, `total`, `currency`, `dueDate` and `hostedInvoiceUrl` (the page where it is paid); a payment adds `paidAt`, a failed payment `reason`, a reminder `daysUntilDue` or `daysOverdue`. A credits event carries `band` (`low` or `empty`), `balance` and `threshold`. A standing event carries `status`, `previousStatus` and `reason`. A storage event carries `reason` and `checkedAt`. Content events (`composition.created`, `widget.published`, `upload.created`) go to your webhook only when subscribed; they do not appear in the dashboard list.

nextBefore.description: Send as `before` to get the next, older page. Null when there is none.

PartnerNotificationDelivery.description: One send of one notification, to one email address or to your webhook. replayOfDeliveryId.description: When this row is a manual replay, the earlier delivery it sent again

PartnerNotificationEvent.description: One kind of event you can be told about.

description.description: One sentence that says when it happens

alwaysEmailed.description: True for money and standing: you are emailed whatever you chose, and can narrow only what your own system receives.

delivery.description: `all`: email (when chosen), dashboard inbox and webhook. `webhook`: signed call only — no email and not listed in the dashboard inbox.

PartnerNotificationDefaultRecipients.description: Who gets the emails while you have given no addresses of your own.

payments.description: For the invoice events, the billing emails of your billing profile, or your contact email when there are none

other.description: For every other event, your contact email

PartnerNotificationSettings.description: Where your notifications go. The secret that signs your webhook is never part of it.

emailRecipients.description: The addresses the emails go to. Empty means the defaults.

webhookUrl.description: Where Widgetic sends a signed call for each event. Null while the webhook is switched off.

events.description: Every event there is, for a settings screen to list

emailRecipients.description: The addresses the emails go to, at most five. An empty list goes back to the defaults.

emailEvents.description: The events you want by email. Null for every event.

domain.description: Domain pattern to allow (supports wildcards like *.example.com)

ManagedUser.description: A managed user as the API answers. The answer names its fields in camelCase (`externalId`), while the request that creates or changes a managed user names them in snake_case (`external_id`).

isActive.description: Whether new compositions, widgets and uploads can be filed under this managed user. `false` means it has been switched off (`updateManagedUser` with `is_active: false`): what it already has stays, and filing anything new under it answers `409 MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`. A record from before the switch existed may answer `null`, which counts as on.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the managed user was created

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the managed user was last updated

external_id.description: Your own identifier for the managed user. Must be unique among the managed users you manage (409 otherwise); another partner using the same value does not matter.

manager_id.description: ID of the user who will manage this managed user. Defaults to your own user ID; a partner can only use their own ID (403 otherwise), only an admin can name another manager.

metadata.description: Additional metadata for the managed user

external_id.description: Updated external identifier for the managed user. Must be unique among the managed users you manage (409 otherwise).

metadata.description: Updated additional metadata for the managed user

is_active.description: Switch the managed user off (`false`) or back on (`true`). A managed user that is off keeps everything already filed under it, and that content can still be listed, but nothing new can be filed under it (`409 MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`). Send a real boolean, not the text "false". Switching a managed user off also ends all of its editor sessions.

surfaces.description: The pieces of Widgetic's editor the session may drive. `files` is the media library (the File Browser: upload a file, list the files uploaded for this user); what a user uploads is kept in your own storage destination. Partner storage is not optional: a session of any surface can be made only once you have set a destination up (`setPartnerStorageDestination`), and is refused with `409 PARTNER_STORAGE_REQUIRED` until then. `editor` is editing one of this user's compositions: read it, change its name, content, design and embed settings, read its schemas, and ask where to show it (`getCompositionPreview`: the widget's published page). `creator` is Widgetic's widget creator, with its drawing canvas and its AI: this user's canvases, the widgets on them, their components and the conversation of each widget, the generation, build and publish calls that make a widget, and the compositions of those widgets (list, make). The surfaces do not imply one another: the whole creator also saves a composition (`editor`) and attaches pictures to its chat (`files`), so ask for `["creator", "editor", "files"]`.

expires_in_seconds.description: How long the session lasts, in seconds. It cannot be extended; make a new session when it ends.

allowed_origin.description: Bind the session to one web page origin, such as `https://app.example.com` (no path; `http` is accepted only for `localhost`). The session is then refused from any other origin, and from a request that carries no `Origin` header. Leave it out for a session that can be used from anywhere, which is what a server-side caller needs.

max_credits.description: The most credits this session may spend on Widgetic's AI, one credit being one generation. Once the operations it ran have taken that many, the next one is refused (402, `EDITOR_SESSION_CREDIT_LIMIT_REACHED`) and the browser is only told that the feature is not available right now. A generation that fails is refunded and does not count. Leave it out to get the limit Widgetic has set for your account, if it has set one (it sets none unless you ask), and otherwise no limit of its own, which leaves the credits of your account as the only ceiling. Send `null` to ask for no limit of its own even when a default is set.

EditorSession.description: An editor session you have just made. `token` is shown once and cannot be read again: hand it to the browser of this one user and keep it out of logs and storage.

token.description: The credential the browser sends as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It starts with `wgt_ses_`. It works only for the calls of the session's surfaces, only for this managed user's content, and only until `expiresAt`.

sessionId.description: Identifies the session, so you can end it (`revokeManagedUserEditorSession`). It is not a credential.

allowedOrigin.description: The web page origin the session is bound to, or null when it is not bound

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Required: a call without it is refused with `400`. A key of your own that names this one request; a UUID is ideal. It is 8 to 50 characters of letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Send the same key again when you retry (after a timeout, a dropped connection or a `5xx`) and the call is carried out once: the retry gets the first answer back, marked `X-Idempotency-Cached: true`. The same key with a different body is refused with `422`, and a retry that arrives while the first call is still running with `409` (see `Retry-After`).

IdempotencyKeyOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyOptional.description: Optional: without it the call is carried out every time it is sent. A key of your own that names this one request; a UUID is ideal. It is 8 to 50 characters of letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Send the same key again when you retry (after a timeout, a dropped connection or a `5xx`) and the call is carried out once: the retry gets the first answer back, marked `X-Idempotency-Cached: true`. The same key with a different body is refused with `422`, and a retry that arrives while the first call is still running with `409` (see `Retry-After`).
